1	---
2	name: code-review
3	description: "Review code changes adversarially for correctness and evidence, with an explicit check that tests, assertions, tolerances, comparators, labels, and gates were not weakened to make the change appear successful. Use whenever reviewing a diff, commit, pull request, test change, validation change, or dispatching an adversarial code review."
4	---
5	
6	# Code review
7	
8	## Purpose
9	
10	Try to refute the change's correctness claims. Inspect the implementation, its
11	tests, and the evidence together. A passing suite is not sufficient when the
12	change also weakens what the suite requires.
13	
14	This skill owns the substance of adversarial code review. Separate skills may
15	set reviewer counts, exact-head attestation, validation authority, and landing
16	policy.
17	
18	## Establish the review target
19	
20	Before reviewing, identify the repository, base revision, exact head revision,
21	and intended behavior. Review the complete diff and the relevant surrounding
22	code and tests. Bind the verdict to the exact head; a changed head requires a
23	fresh review.
24	
25	## Mandatory goalpost-moving check
26	
27	The coordinator applies this check before dispatching an adversarial review and
28	includes this complete block in every adversarial-review prompt, not a pointer
29	to it:
30	
31	> GOALPOST-MOVING REVIEW RULE
32	>
33	> Adversarial reviewers must look explicitly for goalpost moving. We are extremely skeptical of any goalpost moving. YOU DO NOT CLEAR THE BAR BY SIMPLY LOWERING THE BAR.
34	>
35	> Treat each of these as an explicit review target:
36	> - weakening an assertion so a test passes
37	> - widening a tolerance · adding an exemption · skipping a case · relaxing a comparator
38	> - renaming or relabelling so a failure reads as a pass
39	> - deleting a check rather than satisfying it
40	
41	Compare every changed test, threshold, allowlist, skip, label, classification,
42	and gate with the base revision. Determine whether the implementation now meets
43	the original requirement or whether the requirement was changed to admit the
44	implementation. Call out either result explicitly, including when no lowering
45	of the bar is present.
46	
47	## Review method
48	
49	1. Trace the changed behavior through the real execution path. Do not infer
50	   behavior from names, configuration, or successful exit status alone.
51	2. Check the claimed evidence against the exact behavior it is supposed to
52	   prove. Identify missing identity, causation, coverage, or provenance links.
53	3. Inspect production and test changes together. Require a qualifying case to
54	   pass and a violating case to be refused when the change introduces or alters
55	   a guard.
56	4. Report concrete findings with file and line evidence, impact, and the change

---
name: code-review
description: "Review code changes adversarially for correctness and evidence, with an explicit check that tests, assertions, tolerances, comparators, labels, and gates were not weakened to make the change appear successful. Use whenever reviewing a diff, commit, pull request, test change, validation change, or dispatching an adversarial code review."
---

# Code review

## Purpose

Try to refute the change's correctness claims. Inspect the implementation, its
tests, and the evidence together. A passing suite is not sufficient when the
change also weakens what the suite requires.

This skill owns the substance of adversarial code review. Separate skills may
set reviewer counts, exact-head attestation, validation authority, and landing
policy.

## Establish the review target

Before reviewing, identify the repository, base revision, exact head revision,
and intended behavior. Review the complete diff and the relevant surrounding
code and tests. Bind the verdict to the exact head; a changed head requires a
fresh review.

## Mandatory goalpost-moving check

The coordinator applies this check before dispatching an adversarial review and
includes this complete block in every adversarial-review prompt, not a pointer
to it:

> GOALPOST-MOVING REVIEW RULE
>
> Adversarial reviewers must look explicitly for goalpost moving. We are extremely skeptical of any goalpost moving. YOU DO NOT CLEAR THE BAR BY SIMPLY LOWERING THE BAR.
>
> Treat each of these as an explicit review target:
> - weakening an assertion so a test passes
> - widening a tolerance · adding an exemption · skipping a case · relaxing a comparator
> - renaming or relabelling so a failure reads as a pass
> - deleting a check rather than satisfying it

Compare every changed test, threshold, allowlist, skip, label, classification,
and gate with the base revision. Determine whether the implementation now meets
the original requirement or whether the requirement was changed to admit the
implementation. Call out either result explicitly, including when no lowering
of the bar is present.

## Review method

1. Trace the changed behavior through the real execution path. Do not infer
   behavior from names, configuration, or successful exit status alone.
2. Check the claimed evidence against the exact behavior it is supposed to
   prove. Identify missing identity, causation, coverage, or provenance links.
3. Inspect production and test changes together. Require a qualifying case to
   pass and a violating case to be refused when the change introduces or alters
   a guard.
4. Report concrete findings with file and line evidence, impact, and the change
   required to resolve them. Do not substitute a vague procedural objection for
   a technical finding.
5. State a verdict only after resolving the goalpost-moving check and the
   correctness findings against the exact reviewed head.

## Report structure

```text
Review target: <repository> <base>..<exact head>

Findings:
- <severity>: <file:line> — <problem, impact, and required change>

Goalpost-moving assessment:
- Assertions weakened: yes/no — <evidence>
- Tolerance widened, exemption added, case skipped, or comparator relaxed: yes/no — <evidence>
- Failure renamed or relabelled as a pass: yes/no — <evidence>
- Check deleted instead of satisfied: yes/no — <evidence>

Verification: <commands or evidence inspected, with limitations>
Verdict: approve / changes requested
```

Put findings first. If there are no findings, say so explicitly and still
include the goalpost-moving assessment, residual risks, and verification limits.

1	## Review target
2	
3	`rrnewton/hermit` PR https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3047 — base `158a89f6217b25db9540237f9c1e256cdbaf785c` → head **`a88f948021a24c6a1ea808f868516c0691c8819a`**, tree **`cf2185e73d2335ddd70162e336b27440df5bf3d8`**, linked backend Reverie `596b9adee8473dc0a7e62dce18580eead3d0c5c9`.
4	
5	Prior complete source verdict at `a9d3b1fa…`/tree `340e146b…` was **APPROVE** with nonblocking F1 and retained F2–F4; I read its literal text and retain its analysis where the source is unchanged. Only two paths differ from that judgement, and I verified that independently rather than accepting it: `composition-readback.json` binds every one of the 63 source copies to `a88f948…`, and exactly two report `same_bytes_and_mode: false` against the prior reviewed copies — `hermit-cli/tests/cli.rs` and `scripts/validate.rs`. The two supplied diffs' post-image blobs (`297c41ff7e2360dd…` for cli.rs, `3d57645d10d989d4…` for validate.rs) match the blob IDs recorded for those two paths at `a88f948…`, so the diffs I read are the bytes at the reviewed head, not a paraphrase of them.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Findings
10	
11	**Prior F1 is resolved correctly, not bypassed.** `hermit-cli/tests/cli.rs:3477` adds exactly `.current_dir(native_dir.path())` to the ptrace/KVM loop's builder; `base-cli.rs:3474-3479` confirms the pre-change block and that nothing else in the method moved. I re-derived the three resolution questions rather than reusing the prior claim:
12	- The Hermit executable is `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_hermit")` (`cli.rs:207`) and the guest is `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/stdio-inode-identity/stdio_inode_identity` (`cli.rs:455-477`). Both absolute, so cwd cannot affect resolution.
13	- The fixture's pollution mechanism is real and is what the change fixes: `check_reuse` calls `mkstemp("stdio-inode-a-XXXXXX")`/`"…-b-…"` relative to the guest cwd (`tests/c/fixtures/stdio_inode_identity.c:178-180`) and only unlinks them on the success path (`:246`). Both Hermit legs now write into the test-owned `TempDir` instead of the checkout.
14	- The official lane is untouched: `append_hermit_args` → `execution_root_args` injects `--mount=type=tmpfs,target=/test --workdir=/test` before the `--` (`cli.rs:94-105,125-191`), and `--workdir` sets the guest's own directory (`run.rs:722`, asserted at `run.rs:1665-1677`), so the launching process's cwd is irrelevant there.
15	
16	No assertion was touched: `assert_success`, `assert_eq!(stdout…)`, `assert_eq!(stderr(&output), "", "{backend} {mode}")`, the native leg, and the original `/bin/cat` exit-1 / empty-stdout / "bad file descriptor" block are byte-identical.
17	
18	**N1 — MINOR, incoming main, real coverage reduction, named rather than hidden. `scripts/validate.rs:1505-1514` with the caller at `:1695`.** Before, both legs of `submodule_failure_service_result_bracket` ran the *clone's* `./scripts/validate.rs` with `HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED`/`HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT` removed, so both compiled the copied driver through real rust-script. Now only the missing-agent-utils leg does that (`run_fixture(&checkout, None, …)` at `:1647`); the missing-rr leg runs `root/scripts/validate.rs` with prepared selection retained. The property "the copied driver *with* agent-utils present compiles under real rust-script" is therefore no longer exercised by this bracket. It is not lost outright — the parent process executing the bracket *is* the compiled root driver, and the new guard proves the clone's bytes equal root's — but it is a genuine narrowing of incidental coverage and should be read as such, not as a free optimization.
19	
20	**N2 — MINOR, evidence limit of the new guard. `scripts/validate.rs:1343-1426`.** `assert_submodule_fixture_source` establishes *clone ≡ root source* equivalence. It does not establish *prepared executable ≡ root's current source*. The comment at `:1348-1350` ("do not equate a cache name with source") addresses one half of that concern; the other half — an executable published by `build.rust_scripts` (`:7236-7239`, `./ci/prepare-rust-scripts.sh`) that is stale relative to root's working tree because the tree changed after the producer node ran — is undetectable by this helper and would make the fixture exercise older driver logic while reporting a pass. This is a pre-existing property of the prebuilt mechanism that every other graph consumer already has; the change extends it to this fixture. If tightened later, the narrow fix is to compare the published artifact's recorded content hash against the script's current bytes. Not blocking.
21	
22	**N3 — MINOR, behavior change for local dirty runs. `scripts/validate.rs:1362-1396`.** The helper compares *every* tracked non-gitlink path in root's working tree against the clone, and the clone carries root's HEAD content plus a fixed 24-file overlay (`:1558-1583`). A locally dirty checkout with an edit outside that overlay list now makes this node refuse with `original source differs from fixture: <path>`, where it previously ran. That is fail-closed and strictly stricter — the opposite direction from goalpost moving — but it is a real new refusal mode for developers running with `--skip-inner-dirty-working-tree…`, and the overlay list is now load-bearing in a second way.
23	
24	**N4 — Residual limit, explicitly preserved (from `fixture-cwd-REVIEW.md`, which I confirmed against the code).** The loop's cwd is a `TempDir` under `env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")`. With no `--workdir`, the KVM leg resolves the process cwd *after* container setup (`run.rs:2005-2009`) and the container replaces `/tmp` with a private tmpfs, so a custom Cargo target directory below `/tmp` still fails with the documented `kvm_cwd_resolution_error` diagnostic (`hermit-cli/src/lib.rs:1894,1923-1944`). The variable's *name* does not prove visibility; this limitation stands and is not claimed away.
25	
26	**N5 — Nit, no action.** The guest cwd now varies per run (random tempdir suffix) where it was previously the fixed crate directory. Harmless here: this method passes `--strict` without `--verify`, so no cross-run comparator sees it, and the fixture prints no path (it only uses `getcwd` internally at `stdio_inode_identity.c:189` to build an absolute path for the `AT_EMPTY_PATH` control). The native leg already had this property at a9.
27	
28	**Retained from the prior review, not silently repaired or erased:** F2 (SaBRe live discovery still labels any descriptor first seen at slot 0/1/2 as an inherited stream, `tool_local.rs:718` / `:843-850`, unproven-not-regressed), F3 (inherited streams keep the numeric-slot inode on the `fstat` entrypoint only, `files.rs:2669-2676` vs `:2702`, so the stat-route-consistency claim holds for **ordinary objects only**), F4 (`InodePool::new()` starts at 1 while fixed stdio identities are 1000–1002 and `DET_INODE_OFFSET = 9000` has no consumer, so ≥1000 determinized inodes collide — pre-existing, `tool_global.rs:165` / `consts.rs:21,25`). None of the six metadata consumers, the resource guard at `syscalls.rs:48-58`, the mount-provenance helper (`lib.rs:1954-1979`, call site `:1990`, which I re-read at the final head and which still refuses uncaptured-but-nonempty vectors before capture, propagates capture errors, compares with `!=`, and mutates `config` only after every refusal point), or the C fixture changed a byte.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Goalpost-moving assessment
33	
34	- **Assertions weakened: no.** Both changed files add code without removing any condition. The bracket's two diagnoses are intact verbatim: missing agent-utils still requires non-success **and** no result file **and** no `FINAL_VALIDATE_STATUS` in stdout **and** an `agent-utils` mention (`validate.rs:1653-1664`); missing rr still requires exit code exactly `Some(1)`, `FinalValidateStatus::Failed`, `exit_code == 1`, **`executed_nodes == 1`**, and the `pre.submodules` / `third-party/rr` / `FINAL_VALIDATE_STATUS: FAILED` strings (`:1710-1723`). The cli.rs empty-stderr and stdout-equality assertions are untouched.
35	- **Tolerance widened / exemption added / case skipped / comparator relaxed: no — and this is the interesting one.** The plausible cheap fix for a bracket that reuses a 996 KB rust-script driver is to raise the inner `timeout --signal=TERM 300`. That number is unchanged (`:1463`); the argv was only restructured so the script path can be chosen. What the change does instead is remove a redundant recompile and pay for it with a *new* precondition — exact tracked-byte, execute-bit and symlink-target equality plus a clean agent-utils at the exact recorded pin, all fail-closed (`:1358-1359`, `:1391-1395`, `:1417-1423`; a missing `root/agent-utils` fails at `Command::output()` and refuses). That is the harder option, not the cheaper one. The prepared-selection exemption is scoped to exactly the leg that does not test compilation (`:1505-1511`), and the leg that does test it keeps both `env_remove`s.
36	- **Failure renamed or relabelled as a pass: no.** The missing-rr case remains a typed one-node `FAILED`; the missing-agent-utils case remains a pre-driver bootstrap failure that must **not** manufacture a typed result. In cli.rs, the unresolved cat obligation still sits first in the same method, so the new descriptor-reuse legs still cannot report green while it fails.
37	- **Check deleted instead of satisfied: no.** The only deletion in either diff is the two `env_remove` calls' unconditional placement, replaced by a conditional plus a stronger source-identity obligation. Nothing in the fixture-cwd patch is a deletion at all.
38	- **Scope-isolation check I ran myself rather than inheriting:** the concern with running root's driver is that the child could diagnose the *original* tree. `repo_root()` is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the process cwd (`validate.rs:5828-5832`) and `run_fixture` still sets `.current_dir(checkout)` (`:1476`), so the clone is what `pre.submodules` inspects. And the failure mode is loud, not silent: if the child ever resolved root, `pre.submodules` would *pass* there and the bracket's failure-expecting assertions would fire. The private-ledger dev/ino/mode/len/mtime/ctime identity guard (`:1444-1460`, `:1518-1522`) and the full scope/run-state/tool-authority `env_remove` list (`:1481-1504`) are unchanged.
39	
40	---
41	
42	## Linux semantics, determinism, composition
43	
44	No product implementation changed, so the Linux-semantics surface is exactly the prior review's: the fixed-inode domain remains the strict subset `fd ∈ 0..=2 ∧ resource ∈ {ContainerStdin,Stdout,Stderr}`, the KVM mount path replaces a fabricated `0:1` device with exact agreement-or-refuse against the backend's real namespace snapshot, and the F3 cross-route divergence for genuinely inherited streams is retained and disclosed. Determinism: N5 is the only new run-varying quantity and no comparator observes it.
45	
46	Composition: the union is `prior a9 source ⊕ one incoming path ⊕ one 44-byte insertion`. I verified the *relation*, not just counts — the two differing paths in the 63-file readback are exactly the two claimed, the incoming path `scripts/validate.rs` is disjoint from all 21 authored paths, and no authored file was disturbed. The new `#[test] source_and_agent_utils_mismatches_refuse_prepared_reuse` lives in validate.rs's own harness, which carries no pinned population in `NEXTEST_EXPECTED_COUNTS` (`validation_dag_static.rs:202-241`), so it correctly requires no inventory bump and the PR's `test.hermit_unit` 630→634 for `-p hermit --lib --bins` is still exactly the four new `hermit-cli/src/lib.rs` methods. No backend pin, budget, selected population or comparator moves in this follow-up.
47	
48	Small coverage gap in the new guard test, for the record: it covers matching source, changed bytes, changed execute bit, changed symlink target, dirty/untracked/divergent agent-utils and a re-pinned positive case, but not the missing-file `cannot compare` path and not the `160000` gitlink-skip branch.
49	
50	---
51	
52	## Evidence and limits
53	
54	- **No execution of any kind in this review** — Read/Grep only; no build, test, guest, ref, claim or PR operation.
55	- The nineteen selected native methods, fmt, workspace/all-target Clippy, the 634-identity listing, the published CLI build, both descriptor-reuse legs and all three complete-stat-routes legs are real completed measurements **at `aa7ea4827b83…` with the published `a31abf55` binary**, not at this head and not absent. Nothing here relabels them.
56	- **`run_kvm_preserves_closed_standard_input` has still never executed as written, at any head.** The a9 official attempt refused before admission (unpublished a9 unresolvable by the default admission checkout/API; zero tests ran) — that is neither a pass nor a failure. The empty-stderr assertion at `cli.rs:3483` remains the specific uncovered condition, and the F1 line does not change that. The `complete-stat-routes` mode remains a separate mandatory obligation.
57	- Reverie full-library evidence remains **426 pass / 1 fail of 427** on the authenticated candidate ELF, with the unchanged `vm.rs` failure uncaused and no base comparison. Prior historical loader, fdinfo, stat-route and native-control failures stay recorded as failures.
58	- **Does this follow-up create a new necessary validation condition?** Only one, and it is narrow: N1/N2 mean the bracket's missing-rr leg now depends on the prepared-executable path, so the first real execution of `submodule_failure_service_result_bracket` after this lands is the causally relevant check — and that belongs to main's own validation of `158a89f6…`, not to this PR, whose authored paths are disjoint from it. The cli.rs line creates no new condition beyond the already-declared obligation to run the method. I impose no new exact-head whole-DAG receipt.
59	
60	---
61	
62	## Verdict
63	
64	**APPROVE** for exactly `a88f948021a24c6a1ea808f868516c0691c8819a` (tree `cf2185e73d2335ddd70162e336b27440df5bf3d8`).
65	
66	The F1 correction is the minimal, correct fix to the concrete defect I raised, with the official `/test` path, every argument, the strict/minimal environment, stdin setup and all four assertions preserved. The incoming main change reaches the same required boundary by a faster route and pays for it with a fail-closed source-identity precondition rather than with a widened timeout or a deleted check. N1–N3 are nonblocking observations, N4–N5 are preserved limits, and F2–F4 remain open, disclosed and unworsened.

## Review target

`rrnewton/hermit` PR https://github.com/rrnewton/hermit/pull/3047 — base `158a89f6217b25db9540237f9c1e256cdbaf785c` → head **`a88f948021a24c6a1ea808f868516c0691c8819a`**, tree **`cf2185e73d2335ddd70162e336b27440df5bf3d8`**, linked backend Reverie `596b9adee8473dc0a7e62dce18580eead3d0c5c9`.

Prior complete source verdict at `a9d3b1fa…`/tree `340e146b…` was **APPROVE** with nonblocking F1 and retained F2–F4; I read its literal text and retain its analysis where the source is unchanged. Only two paths differ from that judgement, and I verified that independently rather than accepting it: `composition-readback.json` binds every one of the 63 source copies to `a88f948…`, and exactly two report `same_bytes_and_mode: false` against the prior reviewed copies — `hermit-cli/tests/cli.rs` and `scripts/validate.rs`. The two supplied diffs' post-image blobs (`297c41ff7e2360dd…` for cli.rs, `3d57645d10d989d4…` for validate.rs) match the blob IDs recorded for those two paths at `a88f948…`, so the diffs I read are the bytes at the reviewed head, not a paraphrase of them.

---

## Findings

**Prior F1 is resolved correctly, not bypassed.** `hermit-cli/tests/cli.rs:3477` adds exactly `.current_dir(native_dir.path())` to the ptrace/KVM loop's builder; `base-cli.rs:3474-3479` confirms the pre-change block and that nothing else in the method moved. I re-derived the three resolution questions rather than reusing the prior claim:
- The Hermit executable is `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_hermit")` (`cli.rs:207`) and the guest is `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR/stdio-inode-identity/stdio_inode_identity` (`cli.rs:455-477`). Both absolute, so cwd cannot affect resolution.
- The fixture's pollution mechanism is real and is what the change fixes: `check_reuse` calls `mkstemp("stdio-inode-a-XXXXXX")`/`"…-b-…"` relative to the guest cwd (`tests/c/fixtures/stdio_inode_identity.c:178-180`) and only unlinks them on the success path (`:246`). Both Hermit legs now write into the test-owned `TempDir` instead of the checkout.
- The official lane is untouched: `append_hermit_args` → `execution_root_args` injects `--mount=type=tmpfs,target=/test --workdir=/test` before the `--` (`cli.rs:94-105,125-191`), and `--workdir` sets the guest's own directory (`run.rs:722`, asserted at `run.rs:1665-1677`), so the launching process's cwd is irrelevant there.

No assertion was touched: `assert_success`, `assert_eq!(stdout…)`, `assert_eq!(stderr(&output), "", "{backend} {mode}")`, the native leg, and the original `/bin/cat` exit-1 / empty-stdout / "bad file descriptor" block are byte-identical.

**N1 — MINOR, incoming main, real coverage reduction, named rather than hidden. `scripts/validate.rs:1505-1514` with the caller at `:1695`.** Before, both legs of `submodule_failure_service_result_bracket` ran the *clone's* `./scripts/validate.rs` with `HERMIT_PREBUILT_RUST_SCRIPTS_REQUIRED`/`HERMIT_RUST_SCRIPT_ARTIFACT_ROOT` removed, so both compiled the copied driver through real rust-script. Now only the missing-agent-utils leg does that (`run_fixture(&checkout, None, …)` at `:1647`); the missing-rr leg runs `root/scripts/validate.rs` with prepared selection retained. The property "the copied driver *with* agent-utils present compiles under real rust-script" is therefore no longer exercised by this bracket. It is not lost outright — the parent process executing the bracket *is* the compiled root driver, and the new guard proves the clone's bytes equal root's — but it is a genuine narrowing of incidental coverage and should be read as such, not as a free optimization.

**N2 — MINOR, evidence limit of the new guard. `scripts/validate.rs:1343-1426`.** `assert_submodule_fixture_source` establishes *clone ≡ root source* equivalence. It does not establish *prepared executable ≡ root's current source*. The comment at `:1348-1350` ("do not equate a cache name with source") addresses one half of that concern; the other half — an executable published by `build.rust_scripts` (`:7236-7239`, `./ci/prepare-rust-scripts.sh`) that is stale relative to root's working tree because the tree changed after the producer node ran — is undetectable by this helper and would make the fixture exercise older driver logic while reporting a pass. This is a pre-existing property of the prebuilt mechanism that every other graph consumer already has; the change extends it to this fixture. If tightened later, the narrow fix is to compare the published artifact's recorded content hash against the script's current bytes. Not blocking.

**N3 — MINOR, behavior change for local dirty runs. `scripts/validate.rs:1362-1396`.** The helper compares *every* tracked non-gitlink path in root's working tree against the clone, and the clone carries root's HEAD content plus a fixed 24-file overlay (`:1558-1583`). A locally dirty checkout with an edit outside that overlay list now makes this node refuse with `original source differs from fixture: <path>`, where it previously ran. That is fail-closed and strictly stricter — the opposite direction from goalpost moving — but it is a real new refusal mode for developers running with `--skip-inner-dirty-working-tree…`, and the overlay list is now load-bearing in a second way.

**N4 — Residual limit, explicitly preserved (from `fixture-cwd-REVIEW.md`, which I confirmed against the code).** The loop's cwd is a `TempDir` under `env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")`. With no `--workdir`, the KVM leg resolves the process cwd *after* container setup (`run.rs:2005-2009`) and the container replaces `/tmp` with a private tmpfs, so a custom Cargo target directory below `/tmp` still fails with the documented `kvm_cwd_resolution_error` diagnostic (`hermit-cli/src/lib.rs:1894,1923-1944`). The variable's *name* does not prove visibility; this limitation stands and is not claimed away.

**N5 — Nit, no action.** The guest cwd now varies per run (random tempdir suffix) where it was previously the fixed crate directory. Harmless here: this method passes `--strict` without `--verify`, so no cross-run comparator sees it, and the fixture prints no path (it only uses `getcwd` internally at `stdio_inode_identity.c:189` to build an absolute path for the `AT_EMPTY_PATH` control). The native leg already had this property at a9.

**Retained from the prior review, not silently repaired or erased:** F2 (SaBRe live discovery still labels any descriptor first seen at slot 0/1/2 as an inherited stream, `tool_local.rs:718` / `:843-850`, unproven-not-regressed), F3 (inherited streams keep the numeric-slot inode on the `fstat` entrypoint only, `files.rs:2669-2676` vs `:2702`, so the stat-route-consistency claim holds for **ordinary objects only**), F4 (`InodePool::new()` starts at 1 while fixed stdio identities are 1000–1002 and `DET_INODE_OFFSET = 9000` has no consumer, so ≥1000 determinized inodes collide — pre-existing, `tool_global.rs:165` / `consts.rs:21,25`). None of the six metadata consumers, the resource guard at `syscalls.rs:48-58`, the mount-provenance helper (`lib.rs:1954-1979`, call site `:1990`, which I re-read at the final head and which still refuses uncaptured-but-nonempty vectors before capture, propagates capture errors, compares with `!=`, and mutates `config` only after every refusal point), or the C fixture changed a byte.

---

## Goalpost-moving assessment

- **Assertions weakened: no.** Both changed files add code without removing any condition. The bracket's two diagnoses are intact verbatim: missing agent-utils still requires non-success **and** no result file **and** no `FINAL_VALIDATE_STATUS` in stdout **and** an `agent-utils` mention (`validate.rs:1653-1664`); missing rr still requires exit code exactly `Some(1)`, `FinalValidateStatus::Failed`, `exit_code == 1`, **`executed_nodes == 1`**, and the `pre.submodules` / `third-party/rr` / `FINAL_VALIDATE_STATUS: FAILED` strings (`:1710-1723`). The cli.rs empty-stderr and stdout-equality assertions are untouched.
- **Tolerance widened / exemption added / case skipped / comparator relaxed: no — and this is the interesting one.** The plausible cheap fix for a bracket that reuses a 996 KB rust-script driver is to raise the inner `timeout --signal=TERM 300`. That number is unchanged (`:1463`); the argv was only restructured so the script path can be chosen. What the change does instead is remove a redundant recompile and pay for it with a *new* precondition — exact tracked-byte, execute-bit and symlink-target equality plus a clean agent-utils at the exact recorded pin, all fail-closed (`:1358-1359`, `:1391-1395`, `:1417-1423`; a missing `root/agent-utils` fails at `Command::output()` and refuses). That is the harder option, not the cheaper one. The prepared-selection exemption is scoped to exactly the leg that does not test compilation (`:1505-1511`), and the leg that does test it keeps both `env_remove`s.
- **Failure renamed or relabelled as a pass: no.** The missing-rr case remains a typed one-node `FAILED`; the missing-agent-utils case remains a pre-driver bootstrap failure that must **not** manufacture a typed result. In cli.rs, the unresolved cat obligation still sits first in the same method, so the new descriptor-reuse legs still cannot report green while it fails.
- **Check deleted instead of satisfied: no.** The only deletion in either diff is the two `env_remove` calls' unconditional placement, replaced by a conditional plus a stronger source-identity obligation. Nothing in the fixture-cwd patch is a deletion at all.
- **Scope-isolation check I ran myself rather than inheriting:** the concern with running root's driver is that the child could diagnose the *original* tree. `repo_root()` is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the process cwd (`validate.rs:5828-5832`) and `run_fixture` still sets `.current_dir(checkout)` (`:1476`), so the clone is what `pre.submodules` inspects. And the failure mode is loud, not silent: if the child ever resolved root, `pre.submodules` would *pass* there and the bracket's failure-expecting assertions would fire. The private-ledger dev/ino/mode/len/mtime/ctime identity guard (`:1444-1460`, `:1518-1522`) and the full scope/run-state/tool-authority `env_remove` list (`:1481-1504`) are unchanged.

---

## Linux semantics, determinism, composition

No product implementation changed, so the Linux-semantics surface is exactly the prior review's: the fixed-inode domain remains the strict subset `fd ∈ 0..=2 ∧ resource ∈ {ContainerStdin,Stdout,Stderr}`, the KVM mount path replaces a fabricated `0:1` device with exact agreement-or-refuse against the backend's real namespace snapshot, and the F3 cross-route divergence for genuinely inherited streams is retained and disclosed. Determinism: N5 is the only new run-varying quantity and no comparator observes it.

Composition: the union is `prior a9 source ⊕ one incoming path ⊕ one 44-byte insertion`. I verified the *relation*, not just counts — the two differing paths in the 63-file readback are exactly the two claimed, the incoming path `scripts/validate.rs` is disjoint from all 21 authored paths, and no authored file was disturbed. The new `#[test] source_and_agent_utils_mismatches_refuse_prepared_reuse` lives in validate.rs's own harness, which carries no pinned population in `NEXTEST_EXPECTED_COUNTS` (`validation_dag_static.rs:202-241`), so it correctly requires no inventory bump and the PR's `test.hermit_unit` 630→634 for `-p hermit --lib --bins` is still exactly the four new `hermit-cli/src/lib.rs` methods. No backend pin, budget, selected population or comparator moves in this follow-up.

Small coverage gap in the new guard test, for the record: it covers matching source, changed bytes, changed execute bit, changed symlink target, dirty/untracked/divergent agent-utils and a re-pinned positive case, but not the missing-file `cannot compare` path and not the `160000` gitlink-skip branch.

---

## Evidence and limits

- **No execution of any kind in this review** — Read/Grep only; no build, test, guest, ref, claim or PR operation.
- The nineteen selected native methods, fmt, workspace/all-target Clippy, the 634-identity listing, the published CLI build, both descriptor-reuse legs and all three complete-stat-routes legs are real completed measurements **at `aa7ea4827b83…` with the published `a31abf55` binary**, not at this head and not absent. Nothing here relabels them.
- **`run_kvm_preserves_closed_standard_input` has still never executed as written, at any head.** The a9 official attempt refused before admission (unpublished a9 unresolvable by the default admission checkout/API; zero tests ran) — that is neither a pass nor a failure. The empty-stderr assertion at `cli.rs:3483` remains the specific uncovered condition, and the F1 line does not change that. The `complete-stat-routes` mode remains a separate mandatory obligation.
- Reverie full-library evidence remains **426 pass / 1 fail of 427** on the authenticated candidate ELF, with the unchanged `vm.rs` failure uncaused and no base comparison. Prior historical loader, fdinfo, stat-route and native-control failures stay recorded as failures.
- **Does this follow-up create a new necessary validation condition?** Only one, and it is narrow: N1/N2 mean the bracket's missing-rr leg now depends on the prepared-executable path, so the first real execution of `submodule_failure_service_result_bracket` after this lands is the causally relevant check — and that belongs to main's own validation of `158a89f6…`, not to this PR, whose authored paths are disjoint from it. The cli.rs line creates no new condition beyond the already-declared obligation to run the method. I impose no new exact-head whole-DAG receipt.

---

## Verdict

**APPROVE** for exactly `a88f948021a24c6a1ea808f868516c0691c8819a` (tree `cf2185e73d2335ddd70162e336b27440df5bf3d8`).

The F1 correction is the minimal, correct fix to the concrete defect I raised, with the official `/test` path, every argument, the strict/minimal environment, stdin setup and all four assertions preserved. The incoming main change reaches the same required boundary by a faster route and pays for it with a fail-closed source-identity precondition rather than with a widened timeout or a deleted check. N1–N3 are nonblocking observations, N4–N5 are preserved limits, and F2–F4 remain open, disclosed and unworsened.

This approval is **not** a claim that any pending check passed: the appended CLI assertions (notably empty stderr) and the original `/bin/cat` block remain unexecuted, `complete-stat-routes` remains a separate obligation, and the generator `--check` and Hermit unit inventory were measured at aa7, not here.

+                mountinfo_mount_ids: if captured { vec![10, 20] } else { vec![] },
+                mountinfo_mount_ids_captured: captured,
+                fdinfo_unlisted_mount_ids: if captured { vec![700, 701] } else { vec![] },
+                mountinfo_device_rewrites: vec![(libc::makedev(0, 1), libc::makedev(8, 1))],
+                ..DetConfig::default()
+            };
+            for contents in [
+                b"malformed".as_slice(),
+                b"10 20 8:1 / / rw - ext4 /dev/root rw\n10 20 8:1 / / rw - ext4 /dev/root rw\n",
+                b"10 20 8:1 / / rw unknown:7 - ext4 /dev/root rw\n",
+            ] {
+                let mut candidate = config.clone();
+                let before = serde_json::to_value(&candidate).unwrap();
+                let error = prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(&mut candidate, || {
+                    mountinfo_identity_order_from(contents)
+                })
+                .unwrap_err();
+                assert!(format!("{error:#}").contains("malformed /proc/self/mountinfo"));
+                assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&candidate).unwrap(), before);
+            }
+            let mut candidate = config;
+            let before = serde_json::to_value(&candidate).unwrap();
+            let error = prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(&mut candidate, || {
+                Err(std::io::Error::from(std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied).into())
+            })
+            .unwrap_err();
+            assert!(
+                error
+                    .downcast_ref::<std::io::Error>()
+                    .is_some_and(|error| error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied)
+            );
+            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&candidate).unwrap(), before);
+        }
+        assert_eq!(mountinfo_identity_order_from(valid).unwrap(), [10, 20]);
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn kvm_mountinfo_config_refuses_uncaptured_provenance_vectors() {
+        for (listed, unlisted) in [(vec![10], vec![]), (vec![], vec![700])] {
+            let mut config = DetConfig {
+                mountinfo_mount_ids: listed,
+                fdinfo_unlisted_mount_ids: unlisted,
+                ..DetConfig::default()
+            };
+            let before = serde_json::to_value(&config).unwrap();
+            let error = prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config(&mut config, || {
+                panic!("must not overwrite incomplete provenance")
+            })
+            .unwrap_err();
+            assert!(error.to_string().contains("no producer-captured namespace"));
+            assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&config).unwrap(), before);
+        }
+    }

This is a composition follow-up to my own literal APPROVE at `a88f948021a24c6a1ea808f868516c0691c8819a` / tree `cf2185e73d2335ddd70162e336b27440df5bf3d8` (read unedited in `prior-a88-REVIEW.md`). I retain that analysis where the source is unchanged and re-derive only the composition, the three incoming paths, and every interaction they have with the authored change.

---

Identical post-image blobs are byte equality of the result; identical pre-image blobs independently confirm main did not touch those files between `158a89f6` and `231228c0`. `candidate-binding.json` binds the same blob IDs to the supplied source copies at `4392560a`. The two remaining paths differ only as described below.

The specific items I was asked not to take on trust are all present in `complete-hermit.patch` at this head: the original closed-stdin `/bin/cat` exit-1 / "bad file descriptor" block first and unchanged (context at the `@@ -3416,6 +3442,46 @@` hunk), the appended strict descriptor checks with **both** empty-stderr assertions (`assert_eq!(stderr(&native), "")` and `assert_eq!(stderr(&output), "", "{backend} {mode}")`), the F1 owned-cwd correction as exactly `.current_dir(native_dir.path())` on the native leg and the ptrace/KVM loop, the six ordinary-resource metadata guards through `deterministic_stdio_inode_for_resource` (fstat entrypoint, fdinfo, maps `stdio_by_raw_inode`, the anonymous proc-fd identity array, the proc-fd readlink route, and the helper's own bracketing unit test), the strict mount provenance helper `prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config` with its refuse-before-mutate ordering and four unit tests, the exact pin `596b9ade…` at all 33 sites, and the explicit DBT carry with the 1050 effective-job-second threshold and 16-job clamp retained verbatim in both scripts.

**The sole manual conflict was resolved correctly, and both values coexist.** `ACTUAL-CONFLICT.patch` stage entries are base `6a0ab6337` (= `158a` blob), ours `bb779b2d8` (= main231 blob, the post-image in `incoming-main.patch`), theirs `862e17783` (= a88 blob, the post-image in `prior-authored.patch`) — precisely a rebase of the PR commits onto main231, and the conflict is only because `test.regular_crates` and `test.hermit_unit` are adjacent lines. The resolved file at `ci/manifest-plan/src/validation_dag_static.rs:202-241` carries **507** for `test.regular_crates` / `test.regular_crates_on_host` and **634** for `test.hermit_unit` / `test.hermit_unit_on_host`, with the other 34 entries at their prior values (679, 27, 5, 158, 4, 78, 24, 6, 19, 8, 9, 4, 1, 6, 24, …) and the docstring at `:199-201` intact. The `_on_host` pair merged automatically because those two lines are 3 apart, not adjacent.

**The generated DAG is internally consistent with the merged table, which is a real check rather than an assumption.** `ci/manifest-plan/src/validation_dag.rs:1127-1135,1214-1231` collects `NEXTEST_EXPECTED_COUNTS` into a map, **requires exactly 38 entries**, and requires a one-to-one match with each step's typed `NEXTEST_EXPECTED_EXECUTED`, refusing both a missing and an unexpected declaration, and refusing the value in command text. The merged table has exactly 38 distinct tags and the merged `ci/dag/validate.json` has exactly 38 `NEXTEST_EXPECTED_EXECUTED` values, with 507 at lines 7775/61834 and 634 at 7824/61880 — the two incoming edits and the two authored edits land on four distinct nodes ~49 lines apart, which is why git merged the JSON without a conflict. No other `505`/`507` literal exists anywhere in the supplied tree (`scripts/validate.rs`: none; `validation_dag.rs` references the tag by name only), so the "four declarations" scope is complete.

**The incoming count change is disjoint from the PR's count change, and I checked that rather than assuming it.** `test.hermit_unit` runs `-p hermit --features third-party-backends --lib --bins`; `test.regular_crates` runs `--workspace --exclude hermit-detcore --exclude hermit --exclude hermetic_infra_hermit_flaky-tests`. The PR's four new `#[test]` functions are all in `hermit-cli/src/lib.rs` (`kvm_mountinfo_config_preserves_captured_provenance`, `…_captures_validated_ambient_namespace`, `…_refuses_missing_or_malformed_capture`, `…_refuses_uncaptured_provenance_vectors`) — package `hermit`, which regular_crates excludes; 630 + 4 = 634. Main's two schema10 additions live in `ci/manifest-plan`, a workspace member (`Cargo.toml:5`) that regular_crates includes and hermit_unit excludes. I also confirmed the PR adds **no** new test function anywhere else: its detcore additions at `syscalls.rs @@ -58,5 +76,32 @@` and `tool_local.rs @@ -1084,6 +1084,70 @@` are assertions appended **inside existing** `#[test]` bodies, and `cli.rs` adds only a helper `fn stdio_inode_identity_guest()` plus a tail on the existing `run_kvm_preserves_closed_standard_input`. So `test.detcore_unit` 679, `test.hermit_integration` 158, `test.cli` 78, `test.liteinst_strict` 24 and `privileged-test.cli_kvm` 24 correctly stay put.

**The rebase repairs a guard the PR would otherwise have landed broken.** `incoming-main.patch` is the *complete* `158a89f6..231228c0` diff and contains **no test source at all** — only the two count declarations, the two generated values, and one assertion in `liteinst_advanced.rs`. It therefore follows that the regular-crates population was already 507 at `158a89f6` while the declaration said 505: the staleness predates the PR's old base, and the prior-approved head `a88f9480` carried a `test.regular_crates` node that could not pass. Importing main's 507 verbatim is the only correct resolution.

**The PID 2→3 assertion matches the established process construction; I derived it from source rather than accepting an observed value.** The test's command is `hermit --log=info run --backend liteinst --strict --base-env=minimal --mount=type=tmpfs,target=/test --workdir=/test --verify -- /usr/bin/python3 -c …` (`liteinst_advanced.rs:169-181,205-231,295-297`). `--verify` reaches `RunOpts::run_verify` → `with_container(&mut container, || self.run_verify_in_container(…))` (`run.rs:4673-4685`), and `with_container` states and implements that the closure "Runs in the freshly forked container init, not in the caller" (`container.rs:1056-1066`). Inside that container init — PID 1 of the new PID namespace — `run_verify_in_container` calls `init_sync_file_tracing` (`run.rs:4969`), which since commit `1d9c9094dea0e7a4a85bb641165088bded1386bd` calls `equalize_tracing_thread_number()` (`tracing.rs:341-343`), whose own long-standing comment says it exists so "our thread number starts at the same DetTid **3**" as `init_file_tracing` (`tracing.rs:404-408`). The joined helper thread takes TID 2 in that namespace, so the root guest is PID 3. The ordinary (non-verify) path does the same thing — `run_in_container` calls `global.init_tracing()` at `run.rs:4873`, also inside the container fork, reaching `init_stderr_tracing` → the same equalizer (`tracing.rs:456-457`). Before `1d9c9094` the synchronous verify path was the **only** one that skipped the equalizer, i.e. the *only* path that produced PID 2; the old assertion encoded that inconsistency. The head's `tracing.rs` blob `5ff6cc6e0` is exactly the post-image of `1d9c9094` (`tracing-history.patch` index `e4ac01060..5ff6cc6e0`), so nothing has moved in that file since. This change makes the test require the log-mode-independent value, and a regression that removed the equalizer would flip it back to 2 and fail.

**N-A — MINOR, observation, pre-existing and not introduced here.** The guest-visible root PID is 3 rather than the 2 an unwrapped container init would give, because a Hermit-internal logging helper thread consumes the namespace's TID 2. That is deterministic and now uniform across logging modes, but it is an implementation detail leaking into guest-visible state; the comment added by this change (`liteinst_advanced.rs:794-795`) states it accurately. No action for this PR.

**N-B — MINOR, evidence limit on the 507 figure, correctly main's obligation.** An exact count cannot by itself distinguish "two tests added" from "three added and one removed". The supporting evidence is main's own listing — 507 selected, 0 ignored, 0 filtered across 29 binaries, with both new b03 schema10 methods present — recorded in `incoming-commits.txt` and not re-executed here. The exposure is narrowed by the structural fact above (no test source changed in `158a..231`), which confines any masked removal to commits before `158a89f6`; the PR neither can nor should diverge from main's declaration. The supplied `ci/manifest-plan/src/ledger/schema10/tests.rs` contains seven test functions, of which the two appended `focused_*` methods are the plausible pair, but I could not diff that file against its pre-addition state from this package.

**Prior findings retained, unchanged and unworsened** (source identical at this head, same blobs): F2 (SaBRe live discovery labels any descriptor first seen at slot 0/1/2 an inherited stream), F3 (inherited streams keep the numeric-slot inode on the `fstat` entrypoint only, so the stat-route-consistency claim holds for **ordinary objects only** — distinct from, and not repaired by, ordinary replacement-object semantics), F4 (`InodePool::new()` starts at 1 while fixed stdio identities are 1000–1002, so ≥1000 determinized inodes collide), and N1/N3 on `scripts/validate.rs` (blob `3d57645d10d989d4`, unchanged from a88). **N2 stands as I wrote it**: an observation about the scope of one source-equality helper, not an established prepared-producer bypass; I am not manufacturing a mechanism finding from it. N4 (KVM cwd resolution under a `/tmp`-rooted target dir) and N5 (per-run guest cwd, observed by no comparator) remain preserved limits.

---

## Goalpost-moving assessment

- **Assertions weakened: no.** The PID assertion changed one exact value and stayed an exact `assert_eq!` on `fields[0]`; every other condition in `liteinst_strict_verify_python_entropy` is byte-identical — three whitespace-separated fields, entropy length `"8"`, hex string length 16, all-ASCII-hexdigit — as are the helper's requirements that the run exit successfully, print `activation verified (traps=1, hooks=31); Detcore Tool active in ptrace host`, bracket the perf availability message **both ways** against `reverie_ptrace::is_perf_supported()`, print `Success: deterministic. Determinism verified.`, and print the hybrid banner (`liteinst_advanced.rs:303-335`). Nothing in the authored diff lost an assertion either; the cat block and both empty-stderr checks are intact.
- **Tolerance widened, exemption added, case skipped, or comparator relaxed: no.** `verification_strictness()` (`run.rs:2894-2900`) is untouched and still returns `Stripped` for this helper because it passes `--strict`, not `--verify-strict`; that is a pre-existing, disclosed property and **not** a canonical-parity claim — the change does not touch it, `ComparisonOptions`, `compare_logs: true`, or any tolerance. No `#[ignore]`, no filter, no timeout, no resource bound, no selector, no `NEXTEST_PREPARED_BUILD_SELECTION` string, and no command argument moved. The 38-entry registry-size guard is unchanged.
- **Failure renamed or relabelled as a pass: no.** 505→507 is an exact-equality inventory refresh in both directions — a run that produces 506 or 508 still refuses — not a lower bound, a range, or a relaxation, and the declaration's own policy comment ("Update these only after enumerating the corresponding shipped command") is preserved. The obvious cheap alternative, relaxing the guard to `>=` or dropping the node, was not taken. The PID change is the analogous case: a different exact value derived from landed source, not a loosened predicate.
- **Check deleted instead of satisfied: no.** The composition deletes nothing. The only deletions anywhere in the authored patch remain the ones I reviewed at a88 — the fabricated `0:1` device mapping and the `mountinfo_*.clear()` block in `run_kvm`, replaced by `prepare_kvm_mountinfo_config`, which is strictly stricter (it refuses uncaptured-but-nonempty provenance, propagates capture errors, compares captured order with `!=`, and mutates `config` only after every refusal point).

---

## Linux semantics, determinism, complete composition

No product implementation byte changed in this composition, so the Linux-semantics surface is exactly the prior review's: the fixed-inode domain stays the strict subset `fd ∈ 0..=2 ∧ resource ∈ {ContainerStdin,Stdout,Stderr}`, KVM mount identities are bound to the backend's real namespace with agreement-or-refuse, and F3's cross-route divergence for genuinely inherited streams is retained and disclosed. No scheduler, signal, clock, process-construction or logging implementation changed here — the equalizer call the PID assertion depends on is already-landed main source (`1d9c9094`), not part of this PR.

Composition: union = prior a88 authored tree ⊕ main's three-path delta, with the two overlapping count files reconstructed as prior-bytes-with-two-precise-`505`→`507`-replacements. I audited `prepare.py` without running it: it compares whole trees as `{mode, type, object}` maps over all 1726 entries (`assert actual==expected`, not a file count), asserts the incoming path set is exactly the three, asserts the replacement source strings occur exactly twice in `validate.json` and exactly once each in the static table before substituting, and then re-reads each reconstructed path out of the actual head and requires byte equality. The authored-patch comparison it performs is per-path added/deleted line bytes, which is weaker than byte equality — the blob-ID triangulation above is what closes that gap independently. All three author lines (`1789614631`, `1789625771`, `1789629276`) and all three full message bodies are unchanged and in order; only commit IDs and parents moved.

---

## Verification, evidence attribution and limits

- **Read-only.** Read/Grep only: no execution, build, test, guest, service, network, ref, claim or publication. I did not compute any hash myself; byte-level claims rest on the git blob IDs that appear independently in `incoming-main.patch`, `follow-up.diff`, `prior-authored.patch`, `complete-hermit.patch`, `ACTUAL-CONFLICT.json` and `candidate-binding.json`, plus my reading of the complete 1387-line authored patch.
- The nineteen selected native methods, fmt, workspace/all-target Clippy, the 634-identity listing, the published `a31abf55` CLI build, both descriptor-reuse legs and all three complete-stat-routes legs are **completed** measurements at **`aa7ea4827b83…`**, bound to that source. They are neither absent nor executions at `a88f9480` or `4392560a`, and nothing here converts them into missing work.
- **Still pending, unchanged:** the official 24-method CLI validation covering the amended `run_kvm_preserves_closed_standard_input`, including its original `/bin/cat` exit-1 block and the appended empty-stderr condition, and `complete-stat-routes` as a separate obligation. The frozen run `1839` was admitted and then reported `COULD_NOT_RUN` with zero nodes and null test counts after a tool-root refusal — neither a method pass nor a product test failure. Scoping the earlier wording as instructed: the historical **pre-repair** method did run and fail at run `1833`; it is the **current amended** method that has not executed at any head.
- Reverie evidence remains **426 pass / 1 fail of 427** on the authenticated ELF; `vm.rs` is unchanged source and does not establish a base failure or the cause of the retained waiter failure. The earlier 37 selected passes and Clippy are real but are not full-library or Hermit parity.
- **New causally necessary condition created by this composition — one, narrow.** The merged `507 + 634` pair has never been executed together: 634 was measured at aa7 against a 505 table, and 507 was measured by main against a 630 table. The generator/consistency check in `validation_dag.rs:1127-1231` is itself a `ci/manifest-plan` test, i.e. inside the `test.regular_crates` population, so the first real run of `test.regular_crates` (and `_on_host`) at this head is the relevant check, together with the DAG freshness/`--check` node. I verified the pairing structurally (38 registry entries ↔ 38 typed env values, four disjoint nodes, correct values) so the risk is low, but it is not discharged by source reading. I impose **no** new exact-head whole-DAG receipt, and I do not treat the completed aa7 complete-mode, generator or inventory results as missing.
- I did not re-review the unchanged descriptor/procfs/mount mechanisms from scratch; I re-read exactly the code needed to judge the three-path delta and its interactions.

---

## Verdict

**APPROVE** for exactly `4392560a4f6e06f136b5a74b0418294a6cdda28a` (tree `b06a3d19d4e15e31542aeef742d5f81679df2a99`).

The rebase carries the prior-approved authored change forward with byte-identical content on 19 of 21 paths and identical `+`/`-` lines on the two overlapping count files, with all three author lines and messages intact. The single manual resolution keeps both correct values and disturbs nothing else, and the merged table and generated DAG satisfy the repository's own one-to-one 38-entry consistency guard. Neither incoming change lowers a bar: 505→507 is an exact-equality inventory refresh that in fact repairs a guard the old base carried stale, and PID 2→3 is an exact value re-derived from the landed tracing-thread equalizer and the container-init fork ordering, matching what every other logging path already produced.

This approval is **not** a claim that any pending check passed: the amended CLI method (notably its empty-stderr assertion) and the original `/bin/cat` block remain unexecuted, `complete-stat-routes` remains a separate obligation, the 507+634 pair has not been run together, and the aa7 results keep their original source attribution.
